opus.why: Short promo line the audience will read. Needs idiomatic English ('second location on the waterfront'), which Sonnet does reliably with no deep reasoning.

fable.why: One-sentence RU→EN translation of a simple announcement; no nuance a smaller model would miss.

opus.why: Mechanical reformat plus simple interval-to-seconds arithmetic. Medium effort keeps the hour/minute sums accurate.

fable.why: CSV→markdown table with small interval-to-seconds arithmetic; medium guards against rounding slips, no higher model needed.

opus.why: Edit a file with several conversions: fl oz to ml, oz to g, lb, inches to mm, and a judgment call on the '18 pt' board caliper. Needs care to stay accurate and leave the rest untouched.

fable.why: Straight imperial→metric conversions in a file with strict 'touch nothing else'; medium for arithmetic accuracy and instruction adherence.

opus.why: Line breaking with words kept verbatim at natural pauses. Easy, but needs enough attention to count words per line and not alter any words.

fable.why: Line-splitting at pauses with word-count limits and zero word changes; mechanical but needs careful counting.

opus.why: Looks like a trivial rename, but the shorthand object keys ({ userId, ... }) are DB field names. Renaming them blindly changes query logic, so it needs 'userId: accountId'. Catching that trap takes Sonnet-level care.

fable.why: Rename looks mechanical but has a trap: `{ userId }` shorthand in Prisma queries must become `{ userId: accountId }` or logic changes; haiku is likely to miss this.

opus.why: Russian punctuation in public brand copy: dashes ('линейка — это'), colon before the list, commas in compound sentences. The rules are nuanced and mistakes show.

fable.why: Russian punctuation for published brand copy; comma/dash rules in long subordinate clauses are intricate enough that sonnet is the safe floor, low effort suffices.

opus.why: Continues the caption translation. Social copy the audience reads, so it must sound natural in Russian, keep the tone across slides, and leave emoji and hashtags alone.

fable.why: Five short caption translations continuing an established pattern; medium for idiomatic phrasing and keeping emoji/hashtags intact.

opus.why: Purely mechanical format conversion: WEBVTT header, comma to period in timestamps, cue numbers optional.

fable.why: SRT→WebVTT is a header plus comma→dot timestamp swap; purely mechanical.

opus.why: Condensing public brand copy to fit X's 280-character limit while keeping all the key points and the voice. Needs both good copy judgment and an accurate character count.

fable.why: Condensing to a hard 280-char limit while keeping meaning is audience-facing copy with exact counting; sonnet handles both reliably, low effort is enough.
